

 converting row names to column using rownames_to_column:
```{r}
taxa_oct2024 <- data.frame(taxa_oct2024)
taxa1_oct2024 <- taxa_oct2024 %>%
      select(superkingdom, genus, species) #selecting only superkingdom, genus and the linker column species because trying to merge the full ncbi and taxa dfs results in too much memory required/fails to execute... "Match procedure results in an allocation larger than 2^31-1 elements."
```



And finally merging both taxonomy table and blast table using join
```{r}
taxa1_distinct_oct2024 <- distinct(taxa1_oct2024)
#ncbi_taxa <- left_join(x = ncbi, y = taxa1_distinct, by ="species") 

ncbi_taxa_oct2024 <- full_join(x = ncbi_oct24, y = taxa1_distinct_oct2024, by ="species") #lets go with the full join option

save(ncbi_taxa_oct2024, file = "ncbi_taxa_oct2024")
#saving the file for quick reloading later on
load("ncbi_taxa_oct2024")

#searching for specific reads that were found in amr gene hits but are coming up blank for taxa hits:

amr_gene_read_IDS_taxa <- ncbi_taxa_oct2024 %>% 
                      filter (query.acc %in% c("37707c41-4bbb-4a8a-83cf-a1abb3732aab", "23c5c7cd-c58c-4025-ad6b-fd385e9d325b", "e9c3fa42-110d-4e1c-a538-1dbae23e262f", "0161b503-5a02-4aa3-be64-6f5b2ccfd4e6", "c1bff406-fb0c-4ee3-a3a6-ffb5511ae0da")) #all of these genes are here - only 23c5c7cd-c58c-4025-ad6b-fd385e9d325b will be retained at later filtering stages because it is the only one that has gaps less than 5!

```

Filtering the reads in the same way as culture vs nan - October 2024, this is the stringent filtering with weighted means and changes to gap proportion and mismatch proportion:

```{r}

  grey_seal_october2024_taxa_stringent2025 <-  ncbi_taxa_oct2024 %>%
                          filter(superkingdom %in% c("Bacteria", "Eukaryota")) %>%
 # filter(gaps <= 5) %>% #and across the whole dataset, filter out any reads that have gaps more than 5 and
              # filter(mismatches <= 200) %>% #mismatches more than 200
  mutate(proportional_gap_number = gaps/alignment.length) %>%# 7.11.24 adding this as i think gaps set at less than 5 is too harsh for longer reads 
                mutate(proportional_mismatch_number = mismatches/alignment.length) %>% # 7.11.24 adding this as i think gaps set at less than 5 is too harsh for longer reads 
 # filter(gaps <= 5) %>% #and across the whole dataset, filter out any reads that have gaps more than 5 and
               #filter(mismatches <= 200) %>% #mismatches more than 200
                          filter(proportional_gap_number <= 0.10) %>% #here i am saying that there can be up to and including 10% gaps in the alignment 
                           filter(proportional_mismatch_number <= 0.10) %>%
              mutate(alignment.prop = alignment.length/query.length) %>%
              filter(alignment.prop >= 0.25) %>%  # and filter reads to retain only those where at least a quarter of the read is aligning to the subject hit   
              filter(query.length >= 500) %>%
              filter(subject.length >= 100) %>%
                           mutate(species.y = sapply(str_split(species, " "), function(x) paste(x[1:2], collapse = " "))) %>% #this bit of code is just to generate a column called species.y which i have in my other datasets and which gets filtered on later in this block of code
                          group_by (query.acc, subject.tax.ids) %>% # FILTERING STEP 1: by grouping the read with subject tax ids, if the same read hits to multiple species/taxa, all these taxa hits are retained for that read
            
               mutate(evalue_nonzero = ifelse(evalue == 0, 1, evalue), 
                      relative_evalue = ifelse(evalue == 0, 1, min(evalue_nonzero)/evalue_nonzero)) %>%
              mutate(relative_alignment_length = alignment.length/max(alignment.length)) %>%
              mutate(alignment_count = n()) %>% #taxon alignment count within a read 
              
              ungroup() %>%
              group_by(query.acc) %>%
             
              mutate(relative_count = alignment_count/n()) %>% #proportion of read alignments to a taxon
               mutate(weight_score = relative_evalue*relative_alignment_length*(percent.identity/100)) %>%
             filter(weight_score == max(weight_score)) %>%
              filter(relative_count == max(relative_count)) %>%
              slice_sample(n=1) %>%
              ungroup()

save(grey_seal_october2024_taxa_stringent2025, file = "grey_seal_october2024_taxa_stringent2025")
#saving the file for quick reloading later on
load("grey_seal_october2024_taxa_stringent2025")
```
